cq-options.description: A decision's alternatives, rendered as a card grid, for places where the reader picks one. Children are cq-option elements only. With `choose` (which requires an id), the reader clicks a card to pick it: the pick reaches Claude as a `choose` action and wears a green ring until the next version marks it `chosen`.
cq-options.x-example: Paper maps Print the route ahead of time; nothing to charge. Dedicated GPS Offline maps, week-long battery, reversible choice.

cq-option.description: One alternative in a decision. Lead with a <strong> title; prose follows. `recommended` draws the accent ring (the author's take); `chosen` the green one (the reader's pick — the choose upgrade sets it live, and the next version carries it). `effort`/`risk` — the cost and the danger of picking this option — render as chips.

cq-plan.description: A plan container owning the chrome plan pages hand-build: lead with a <strong> title, optionally a <dl class="facts"> summary row, then <section> children whose h2 headings number themselves. Content is open — sections, prose, and other widgets nest freely.
cq-plan.x-example:
Rebuilding the aviary feeders
Owner
groundskeeping
Window
before the spring migration

Scope

Four feeders, one season.

Rollout

One feeder a week.

cq-milestones.description: A timeline of milestones with status dots on a rail. Children are cq-milestone elements only.
cq-milestones.x-example: Survey the sites Map sun and squirrel routes. Build the feeders Two classic, two heated. Install and watch

cq-milestone.description: One milestone. Lead with a <strong> title; prose follows. `status` colors the timeline dot; `when` is a free-text schedule label; `tags` is a comma-separated list rendered as chips.

cq-timeline.description: A chronological event log — the incident-report shape. Children are cq-event elements only. Where cq-milestones tracks planned work by status, cq-timeline records what happened, when.
cq-timeline.x-example: Feeder camera offline Battery alert from the north feeder. Battery swapped Camera back Feed resumed.

cq-event.description: One event on a timeline. Lead with a <strong> title; prose follows. `at` is a free-text time label; `kind` colors the dot.

cq-compare.description: Labeled variants side by side — neutral exhibition, where cq-options is a decision. Children are cq-variant elements only.
cq-compare.x-example: Cedar Weathers silver; no sealant. Pine Cheaper; seal it yearly.

cq-variant.description: One variant in a comparison. Lead with a <strong> label; any content follows, widgets included.

cq-metrics.description: A KPI row. Children are cq-metric elements only.
cq-metrics.x-example:
<cq-metrics>
  <cq-metric id="k-visits" value="312" delta="+41" direction="up-good">daily visits</cq-metric>
  <cq-metric id="k-refills" value="2.1/wk" delta="+0.4" direction="up-bad">refills</cq-metric>
  <cq-metric id="k-species" value="14">species seen</cq-metric>
</cq-metrics>

cq-metric.description: One metric: element text is the label, `value` the headline number, `delta` a signed change (leading + or -), `direction` says which sign is good (up-good, up-bad) so the delta colors honestly; without it the delta stays neutral.

cq-ref.description: An inline reference to a source location, rendered as a link. `src` is path or path:line. The link base is resolved once per page from <meta name="cq-base" content="https://host/repo/blob/main/{path}#L{line}">; without that meta the reference renders as plain code.

cq-diff.description: A unified diff rendered with per-file collapse, add/del coloring, and per-file +/− counts. The body is data: the diff verbatim, at column 0 (context lines keep their leading space), with < and > escaped as < and >. Comments anchor to the required id.
cq-diff.x-example:
<cq-diff id="mount-diff">
diff --git a/feeders/mount.py b/feeders/mount.py
--- a/feeders/mount.py
+++ b/feeders/mount.py
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 def bracket():
-    return "plastic"
+    return "steel"
</cq-diff>

cq-tree.description: A file tree from an indent-notation body: one node per line, children indented deeper, a trailing / marking a directory, trailing +N/-N tokens rendering as change badges. Body is data — text only.
cq-tree.x-example:
<cq-tree id="feeder-tree">
feeders/
  mount.py  +2 -2
  schedule.py  +1
  sites/
    north.toml
</cq-tree>

cq-code.description: An annotated code block — the walkthrough shape. The body is the code verbatim (data, < and > escaped, column 0); `hi` highlights line ranges ("3-5,8"); cq-note children anchor remarks at lines.
cq-code.x-example:
<cq-code id="bracket-walk" hi="2">
def bracket(temp):
    if temp < 0:
        return "steel"
    return "cedar"
<cq-note at="2">Freezing is the only threshold that matters.</cq-note>
</cq-code>

cq-note.description: A remark anchored at a line of its cq-code parent. Prose content; `at` is the 1-based line number.

cq-diagram.description: A diagram rendered from a mermaid-source body (flowchart, sequence, state…). The body is data, not prose: text only, angle brackets escaped as < and >. Comments anchor to the required id, not to text inside the SVG.
cq-diagram.x-example:
<cq-diagram id="checkout-flow">
graph LR
  Cart --> Pay
  Pay --> Receipt
</cq-diagram>

cq-board.description: A kanban board the reviewer edits directly: cards drag between columns or reorder within one, and each drop reaches Claude as a `move` action naming the card, target column, and position. Children are cq-column elements only. The next version's markup carries the moved card — the document is the state.
cq-board.x-example: Heated perch Wire the south feeder. Squirrel baffle Camera mount

cq-column.description: One column on a board. `label` is the column heading; cards stack beneath. Children are cq-card elements only; an empty column is a valid drop target.

cq-card.description: One card on a board. Lead with a <strong> title; prose follows. The reviewer drags it by its grip; the id names it in `move` actions and keeps comment anchors stable across moves.

$idioms.description: Recurring shapes the theme styles directly — no registry entry, no JS. Plain semantic HTML gets the theme's voice for free; these classes cover what HTML lacks an element for.

.eyebrow.description: A small-caps label above a heading.

.lede.description: The opening paragraph, set slightly larger.
.lede.example: One paragraph saying what this page decides.

.callout.description: An aside set off from the prose — a tinted field with a hairline border.
.callout.example: <aside class="callout">Rollback is one flag flip; the backfill is idempotent.</aside>

.facts.description: A label/value grid for summary facts, as a definition list.

ol.steps.description: An ordered procedure with numbered markers.
ol.steps.example:
1. Backfill the new store.
  2. Verify counts, then flip reads.

details.description: Evidence: a claim as the <summary>, its backing collapsed beneath. Native disclosure; find-in-page reaches the collapsed content.
details.example:
The parser drops the slash on self-closed custom tags 
document.querySelector("cq-ref").textContent
